summary: Scoped verification of obstacle multi-select bug fix. 10 of 11 sub-checks pass. Primary multi-select behavior, persistence, dashboard rendering, and error validation all work correctly. However, LEGACY MIGRATION is broken: when localStorage contains legacy `assessment.obstacle` string (no `obstacles` key), it is NOT migrated to `obstacles: [value]` — the value is silently dropped and the dashboard shows 'unnamed.'.

integration_issues.issue: storage.js `normalize()` spreads `blankAssessment` (which sets `obstacles: []`) BEFORE checking for legacy `obstacle` string. So `Array.isArray(assessment.obstacles)` is always true after the merge, the migration branch never executes, and the legacy `obstacle: 'Procrastination'` value is discarded. Dashboard shows 'unnamed.' and localStorage still has `obstacle` key (never re-saved).

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/src/logic/storage.js `normalize()`: check `state.assessment.obstacles` (raw) OR the legacy `obstacle` key BEFORE merging with blankAssessment. Suggested patch: derive obstacles from `state.assessment.obstacles` if array, else from `state.assessment.obstacle` string if present, else `[]`; then merge. Example: `const rawObstacles = Array.isArray(state.assessment.obstacles) ? state.assessment.obstacles : (typeof state.assessment.obstacle === 'string' && state.assessment.obstacle.trim() ? [state.assessment.obstacle] : []); const assessment = { ...blankAssessment, ...state.assessment, obstacles: rawObstacles }; delete assessment.obstacle;`
Optionally persist the normalized state back to localStorage on load so the `obstacle` legacy key is cleaned up on disk (currently only cleaned in-memory).
critical_code_review_comments: storage.js normalize() has a merge-order bug: `{ ...blankAssessment, ...state.assessment }` fills `obstacles: []` from defaults, causing the `!Array.isArray` legacy-migration guard to never trigger.
Rest of the multi-select implementation is clean: proper checkbox semantics, aria hint, kebab-case data-testids, error message + disabled state, array-safe consumers, dashboard chip list.
seed_data_creation: Manually seeded a legacy-shaped localStorage payload via page.evaluate to test migration path.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Only the legacy migration path needs re-verification. To reproduce: set localStorage['life-upgrade-ai-state'] with `assessment.obstacle` as a string (no `obstacles` key) and `completed: true`, reload, then check biggest-obstacle-value and localStorage. Everything else (multi-select UX, persistence, dashboard rendering, validation message, disabled state, all 8 options with correct kebab data-testids, deep-dive round-trip) is verified passing.
rca of the issue: In /app/frontend/src/logic/storage.js, normalize() does `const assessment = { ...blankAssessment, ...state.assessment };` first. Because blankAssessment defines `obstacles: []`, the merged assessment ALWAYS has `obstacles` as an array (empty if not provided in raw state). The subsequent `if (!Array.isArray(assessment.obstacles))` guard is therefore never true for legacy payloads (which have `obstacle` as string but no `obstacles` key), so the migration code that reads `state.assessment.obstacle` and populates `assessment.obstacles = [state.assessment.obstacle]` never runs. Legacy user data is silently lost. Mitigation: read raw obstacles/obstacle from `state.assessment` BEFORE merging with defaults, or check `state.assessment.obstacles` (pre-merge) instead of the merged copy.
